_comment: A first draft, not an answer. The collision policy is the server owner's decision, so
this file is that decision written down as data -- and it is deliberately crude.
Rules match on MEASURED GEOMETRY, never a family name. Nothing here knows what a wall
or a slab is; a wall and a bespoke cross of the same shape get the same treatment.
Rules are tried in order and the first match wins, so a specific rule goes above a
The two rules here are the two the game's own behaviour suggests. A plate a pixel
thick is given no collision, which is what Minecraft does with pressure plates and
why their visual geometry costs 196 cubes. Everything else collides as drawn, which
is the naive starting point and the thing to argue with: run `paperized compile` and
the report shows what it costs.
